description:
About Karbon

Karbon is the global leader in AI-powered practice management software for accounting firms. We provide an award-winning cloud platform that helps tens of thousands of accounting professionals work more efficiently and collaboratively every day. With customers in 40 countries, we have grown into a globally distributed team across the US, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the Philippines. We are well-funded, ranked #1 on G2, growing rapidly, and have a people-first culture that is recognized with Great Place To Work® certification and on Fortune magazine's Best Small Workplaces™ List.

We are hiring a Senior Manager of Revenue Operations Systems to lead the team that owns Salesforce across Sales, Marketing, and the Customer organization, and to own the technology stack that powers our sales team. This person sets the architecture and standards for our core GTM platform, runs the team's intake and allocation, and makes sure every tool we pay for earns its place.

This is a player-coach role. Expect roughly half your time building: designing solutions, shipping complex configuration, and reviewing the architecture your team delivers. The other half goes to leading a team of three Revenue Operations Analysts, managing the team's workload, and partnering with GTM leaders so the right work gets done in the right order. We are looking for someone who is the most capable technical operator in the room and gets real energy from making the people around them better. As the function grows, so will the scope of this role.

Karbon is building an agentic organization. Every role here is expected to operate with an AI-first mindset, and this role carries a specific expectation: grow your team's capacity faster than its headcount. The rest of this JD describes what that looks like for Salesforce and the sales technology stack.

About the Role

Salesforce Platform Leadership

  • Own Salesforce as the core GTM platform for Sales, Marketing, and the Customer organization, including the data model, lifecycle automation, sharing and security model, and release management. Set the platform standards and architecture principles your team builds to
  • Design and ship solutions end to end, from complex flows and record types to integrations. Review and approve architectural changes from your team and others, and hold a high bar on quality, documentation, and change management
  • Architect how Salesforce connects to the rest of the GTM stack. Own integration patterns (native, middleware, event-driven) and know when to use each. Build with observability in mind so issues are caught before the business feels them
  • Partner with the Senior Manager of Marketing Operations on the data flow between marketing systems and Salesforce, including campaign sync, lead and contact routing, and attribution field architecture

Sales Technology Stack

  • Own the sales technology stack, including sales engagement, conversation intelligence, data enrichment, and quoting tools, along with the integrations that connect them to Salesforce. Run vendor evaluations, implementations, renewals, and consolidation analyses
  • Keep technology aligned to how Sales, Marketing, and the Customer organization work. Stay close enough to each team to understand their workflows, translate their needs into the right systems decisions, and say no when a new tool is not the answer
  • Make build vs. buy vs. automate decisions with business-case rigor. Identify redundancies, integration gaps, and where AI can remove manual work across the stack. The expectation is to continuously improve how the sales organization is enabled by technology, not just maintain what we have
  • Maintain the tech stack inventory, ownership, and renewal calendar for your domain so leadership and Finance always know what we use, what it costs, who owns it, and what it returns

Data Quality & Governance

  • Own data governance for the Salesforce platform: field definitions and ownership, stage gate enforcement, validation, and dashboard accuracy. Every field has a definition and an owner, and the numbers leaders see can be trusted
  • Run the change management and release process that keeps Salesforce stable as it scales. Enforce scope and intake boundaries without needing escalation
  • Surface issues before they are reported. Connect symptoms to root causes across systems, and frame findings in terms of revenue impact and a proposed action

Team Leadership & Workload Management

  • Lead and develop a team of three Revenue Operations Analysts: two focused on Salesforce and connected tools, and one supporting the Customer organization (customer success, service delivery, and support). Coach through weekly 1:1s and semi-annual reviews, build development plans tailored to each person, and grow people into bigger scope
  • Own the performance process for your team: goal setting, mid-year and annual reviews, calibration, and merit and promotion cases. Address underperformance early and directly
  • Own intake, prioritization, and allocation for the team. Publish the queue, manage to defined SLAs, and make the Now/Next/Later call with the Director of Revenue Operations as a partner. Push back on low-ROI work and reallocate toward the highest-leverage activity
  • Run capacity planning for your team. Every headcount ask is justified through the agentic lens: what AI has already taken on, what still needs a person, and why. Design AI-augmented workflows as the default for new work and teach your team to do the same
  • Own hiring for your team as roles open: write the JD, run the interview loop, and build onboarding that gets new hires productive quickly
  • Codify tribal knowledge into documented processes and runbooks. Remove single points of failure on the team, including yourself

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Be a trusted partner to Sales, Marketing, and Customer leaders at the Director and VP level. Translate their questions into the systems and data changes that answer them, and communicate in business terms
  • Own the roadmap for Salesforce and the sales technology stack, and sequence it against the GTM plan. Present priorities and progress to GTM leadership monthly
  • Lead multi-quarter, cross-functional initiatives end to end. Keep stakeholders informed before they have to ask, and never surprise anyone on delivery

About You!

  • 8+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or Salesforce administration in a B2B SaaS environment, including at least 2 years leading a team. You are as comfortable building a complex flow yourself as you are walking the CRO through the roadmap
  • Deep Salesforce expertise. You have personally built and scaled Salesforce at a growing company and understand the architecture beneath the UI: data model, sharing and security, automation, APIs, and release management. Experience supporting post-sale teams in Salesforce is a strong plus
  • Cross-platform breadth. You have owned Salesforce alongside at least three integrated GTM platforms (e.g., sales engagement, conversation intelligence, marketing automation, data enrichment, CPQ) and can speak to how data moves between them
  • A track record of owning a tech stack. You have run evaluations, implementations, renewals, and consolidations, and can point to tools you added, tools you cut, and why
  • A people leader who grows people. You have coached analysts or admins into bigger scope, handled hard performance conversations with clarity, and managed a shared queue with competing priorities from multiple teams
  • Revenue literacy. You understand the full revenue engine, from new business to expansion, retention, and churn, and you prioritize by revenue impact. You can defend why one request matters more than another in terms a revenue leader accepts
  • Operational rigor with architectural thinking. You balance urgency in fixing what is broken today with a clear vision for what the system needs to look like at 2x and 5x scale
  • An AI-first operator. You are using AI in your work today, you have shipped AI-assisted workflows that expanded real capacity, and you have a point of view on how AI reshapes Revenue Operations
  • Clear, direct communicator. Tight for executives, detailed for peers, and willing to push back when the work calls for it
  • Experience in accounting, professional services, or practice management software is a plus but not required

Why Work at Karbon?

  • Industry-leading benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and up to three eligible dependents. Also:
    • Work-from-home allowance
    • Rice subsidy
    • Meal allowance per working day
    • Laundry allowance
  • 15 paid time off days per year (which includes 5 Karbon Days per year)
  • 7 Sick leave days per year
  • Internet and work-from-home subsidy
  • Discretionary bonus program
  • Work with (and learn from) a very experienced team
  • Be part of a startup team that will continue to grow around you
  • Flexible approach to work environment (we believe in trust and autonomy)
  • A culture of open communication, consistent feedback, and full transparency into company results, metrics, and financial position

Please be aware that Karbon will only contact you via email from our domain, karbonhq.com. If you receive an email from any other domain, please do not click any of those links.

Karbon embraces diversity and inclusion, aligning with our values as a business. Research has shown that women and underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single criteria. If you've made it this far in the job description but your past experience doesn't perfectly align, we do encourage you to still apply. You could still be the right person for the role!

We recruit and reward people based on capability and a performance-driven mindset. We do not discriminate based on race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, lifestyle, age, educational background, national origin, religion, physical or cognitive ability, and other diversity dimensions that may hinder inclusion in the organization.

If there are any adjustments or accommodations that we can make to assist you during the recruitment process and your journey at Karbon, contact us at people.support@karbonhq.com for a confidential discussion. Please note that, due to the volume, emails sent to this email address that are not for adjustments or accommodations will not receive a response.

 

At this time, we request that agency referrals are not submitted for this position. We appreciate your understanding and encourage direct applications from interested candidates. Thank you!
